name: Reuel
overview: Reuel was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as the son of Ibnijah. The biblical record provides limited information about him beyond his lineage. There are no additional notes or distinguishing details about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Reuel means "friend of G-d [El]," indicating a relationship or closeness to God as understood in the Hebrew context. This proper name was not given directly by God but reflects a meaningful theophoric element common in biblical names.
familyAndRelationships: Reuel is explicitly recorded as the son of Ibnijah. It is also inferred that he was the father of Shephatiah. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Reuel's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Benjamin, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:8. This connection situates him within the broader narrative of Israel's tribal history and lineage, underscoring the faithfulness of God's covenant people through their descendants. While not a prominent figure in biblical events, his mention preserves the continuity of the Benjaminite line.
